claim: The Court considered that Israel’s policies and practices, including maintenance and expansion of settlements, construction of associated infrastructure and application of Israeli law, entrenched its control and amounted to annexation of large parts of the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
legal_characterization: Final finding in a non-binding ICJ advisory opinion; not a criminal judgment.
source_organization: International Court of Justice
source_title: Legal Consequences arising from the Policies and Practices of Israel in the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, Advisory Opinion of 19 July 2024

title: ICJ advisory finding on natural resources
summary: The Court assessed Israel’s exploitation of natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory.
claim: The Court concluded that Israel’s use of natural resources in the Occupied Palestinian Territory was inconsistent with its obligations under international law as an occupying Power.
legal_characterization: Final finding in a non-binding ICJ advisory opinion.

title: ICJ advisory finding on Palestinian self-determination
summary: The Court addressed the effect of Israel’s policies and practices on Palestinian self-determination.
claim: The Court concluded that Israel’s prolonged occupation, settlement policy, annexation and related policies and practices obstruct the Palestinian people’s exercise of its right to self-determination.
legal_characterization: Final finding in a non-binding ICJ advisory opinion.

title: ICJ indicates provisional measures in South Africa v. Israel
summary: The International Court of Justice indicated provisional measures while expressly stating that it was not deciding the merits of South Africa's genocide claims.
claim: At the provisional-measures stage, the Court found that at least some rights South Africa claimed under the Genocide Convention were plausible and that there was a real and imminent risk of irreparable prejudice; it ordered Israel to take specified measures pending a merits decision.
legal_characterization: Provisional measures under Article 41 of the ICJ Statute in proceedings under the Genocide Convention; no final determination that genocide occurred.
source_organization: International Court of Justice
source_title: Order of 26 January 2024, Application of the Genocide Convention in the Gaza Strip (South Africa v. Israel)
source_quote: The Court considers that there is urgency, in the sense that there is a real and imminent risk that irreparable prejudice will be caused
verification_notes: Verified against the operative order and its jurisdiction, plausibility, prejudice, and operative sections. Paragraph 30 says the Court was not called upon at this stage to establish breaches of Genocide Convention obligations. The record therefore does not state that the Court found genocide, or that the merits have been decided.

claim: The Court reaffirmed that Israeli settlements in the West Bank and East Jerusalem, and the regime associated with them, have been established and are being maintained in violation of international law.

summary: The Court assessed Israel’s response to violence by settlers against Palestinians.
claim: The Court concluded that Israel’s systematic failure to prevent or punish attacks by settlers against Palestinians, as well as its excessive use of force against Palestinians, was inconsistent with its international obligations.
legal_characterization: Final finding in a non-binding ICJ advisory opinion; not an assignment of individual criminal responsibility.

title: ICJ advisory finding on systemic discrimination
summary: The Court assessed legislation and measures differentiating between settlers and Palestinians in occupied territory.
claim: The Court concluded that Israel’s legislation and measures imposed and served to maintain a near-complete separation between settler and Palestinian communities in the West Bank and East Jerusalem and constituted a breach of Article 3 of CERD.
legal_characterization: Final finding in a non-binding ICJ advisory opinion; not a criminal judgment.

title: ICJ advisory conclusion on obligations of other States
summary: The Court stated consequences for other States arising from Israel’s unlawful continued presence.
claim: The Court concluded that all States are under an obligation not to recognize as legal the situation arising from Israel’s unlawful presence in the Occupied Palestinian Territory and not to render aid or assistance in maintaining that situation.
legal_characterization: Final conclusion in a non-binding ICJ advisory opinion.

title: UN Commission finding on cultural destruction and self-determination
summary: The Commission assessed the combined effect of attacks on education, cultural and religious sites on Palestinian collective identity and self-determination.
claim: The Commission concluded on reasonable grounds that destruction of education and cultural and religious sites, restrictions on access and erasure of heterogeneous history violated the Palestinian people's right to self-determination.
legal_characterization: International-law finding by a UN commission of inquiry; not a judicial judgment.
source_organization: United Nations Independent International Commission of Inquiry on the Occupied Palestinian Territory, including East Jerusalem, and Israel

title: UN Commission finding on four genocidal acts in Gaza
summary: The Commission published a Genocide Convention legal analysis of Israeli authorities' and security forces' conduct in Gaza since October 2023.
claim: The Commission concluded on reasonable grounds that Israeli authorities and security forces committed and continued to commit four genocidal acts: killing, serious bodily or mental harm, destructive conditions of life and measures intended to prevent births.
legal_characterization: Genocide-related legal finding by a UN commission of inquiry under its reasonable-grounds standard; not an ICJ judgment or final judicial determination of state responsibility.

title: UN Commission finding on genocidal intent in Gaza
summary: The Commission assessed direct statements and the overall pattern of conduct in determining the mens rea element of genocide.
claim: The Commission concluded that statements by Israeli authorities were direct evidence of genocidal intent and that the total pattern of conduct supported genocidal intent as the only reasonable inference.
legal_characterization: Mens rea finding by a UN commission of inquiry in its Genocide Convention analysis; not an ICJ merits judgment or final judicial determination.

title: UN Commission conclusion on State responsibility for genocide in Gaza
summary: The Commission stated its conclusion on State responsibility after applying its Genocide Convention analysis to conduct in Gaza.
claim: The Commission concluded that the State of Israel bears responsibility for failure to prevent genocide, commission of genocide and failure to punish genocide against Palestinians in the Gaza Strip.
legal_characterization: State-responsibility conclusion by a UN commission of inquiry; not a final merits judgment of the International Court of Justice.

title: UN Commission finding on incitement to genocide by Israeli officials
summary: The Commission assessed statements by senior Israeli political officials as part of its Genocide Convention legal analysis.

legal_characterization: Incitement-to-genocide finding by a UN commission of inquiry; not a criminal conviction or judicial judgment against the named individuals.
